text: You're new. Wren's already talking at you, so you'll know about the Cup by now.
Come back when she's finished. Then we'll play.
Kesh. Twelve kyu, and I'd like that on the record before we start.
Nine by nine, even game. We'll do it properly -- nigiri. I take a handful of stones, you call odd or even, and whoever's right picks their colour.
Black moves first, which is worth about five and a half points, which is exactly why White gets five and a half points of komi. That's the whole of the arithmetic.
So. Are we playing, or are we going to talk about playing?
Take two. The board isn't going anywhere and neither, apparently, are you.
Right.
I know exactly where that went wrong for me and I am not going to tell you, because you'll only do it again.
That was a real win. I'm saying that once and then I'm going to go and be quietly furious by the kettle.
Hana was watching, by the way. She watches everything. Go and talk to her -- she'll have something for you.
Twice. Twice! Fine. You're not a beginner any more, you're a problem.
Again. Now.
That's the game. You know where it went now, so I'm not going to say it twice.
Which is what everyone does at your strength, by the way. It's what I did for a year.
Hana was watching from the counter. She always is. Go and speak to her, she likes a fresh disaster.
Another? Say the word. I've got all afternoon and a long memory.

exit.intro: Thirteen again. I've been reading about corners.

text: Later, then. I'll be here. Obviously I'll be here.

actions: The club has you on the ladder at 22 kyu.
text: Hold on. Before you go anywhere -- that was a rated game, so it goes on the hooks. Tomas writes them up whether you ask him to or not.
Twenty-two kyu. Everyone starts there and everyone resents it. It isn't an insult, it's a starting position.
You came. I said you would and Wren said you wouldn't, so I have won something already this week.
I enrolled the same day. Bottom of the lower league, same as you, which means the board has us next to each other where everyone can see.
I am going to be above you on it. I want that said out loud at the start so there is no confusion later.
League game? It counts here. That is the entire appeal.

exit.intro: Thirteen. Don't be careful, be right.

text: Hold on. Before anything else -- I cut you in that game and you let the pieces die, and that is the single thing standing between you and being a nuisance to me.
A group on one liberty is not dead. It is nearly dead. Ten minutes and you will never lose one of those again.
Right. You can run. Now the half that stops you having to.
I cut. Everyone tells you that like it is a warning. It is actually an instruction -- watch where I do it and you will know where your own shape is thin.
Right. So it was never dead, it was just badly. There is a difference and it is worth about twenty points a game to you.
Next time I cut you, run. Do not sit there counting. You can count afterwards, at length, in your own time.
Good. Now you know both halves, which means I have to find a new way to beat you and that is genuinely irritating.
I am not being modest. I have one idea and I have just given you it.
There's a thirteen-by-thirteen in the study hall now. Marguerite put it out weeks ago and nobody has touched it, because everyone here is extremely brave until the board gets bigger.
I've played four on it. Lost four. I'm telling you that before you find out, so it counts as honesty rather than as you catching me.
Nine by nine you can bluff -- there's nowhere to hide a mistake and nowhere to hide from one either. Thirteen has corners. You can be wrong in a corner for forty moves before anybody tells you.
